During the day, you can spend almost all your time along the coast: walking, enjoying the water, surfing and admiring the natural scenery. In the evening, restaurants and bars come alive with local music, including forró.

Pipa is well suited to a relaxed ending after a busy sightseeing itinerary. Via Natal Airport, it is easy to combine a stay here with other regions of Brazil or the next stage of a journey through Argentina.

Praia do Forte lies on the coast of Bahia, about 85 km from Salvador. Long beaches, palm trees and mangrove vegetation make it a pleasant place to spend several quiet days by the ocean.

Besides relaxing on the beach, visitors can plan surfing, underwater activities and coastal walks. Sea turtle conservation projects and the ruins of the Garcia de Ávila complex are also of particular interest.

Praia do Forte makes a natural stop after Salvador. A few days by the ocean provide a pause between the city sights of Bahia and the next part of a longer journey through Brazil.

At Praia Vermelha, Rio fits into one small bay: a strip of sand, blue-green water and granite mountains rising above the shore. You can walk by the surf, stop for a photograph and watch the cable cars move above the slopes. With Sugarloaf Mountain so close, even a short stop by the water becomes part of a wider introduction to the city.

The beach is in the Urca neighbourhood, next to the lower cable car station. Its name means "Red Beach". The shoreline here is more compact than Rio's long ocean beaches, with mountains rising much closer to the water. The scenery is especially appealing for a walk before heading up to the viewpoints or after returning from the summit.

On Ada Tours itineraries, Praia Vermelha often features on the day dedicated to Sugarloaf Mountain: from here, the cable cars first travel to Morro da Urca and then higher up. The time spent on the beach itself depends on the excursion programme. If you would like to linger by the sea, you can discuss that while planning the day. Walking, photography and relaxing on the sand are good ways to enjoy the bay; swimming possibilities depend on conditions on the day of your visit.

Preguiças Lighthouse stands in the settlement of Mandacaru in the state of Maranhão. On the tour itinerary, it is listed as "Pergula Lighthouse".

A stop at the lighthouse is part of a boat trip along the Preguiças River. The observation platform offers views of the river and coastal landscapes. Historically, the lighthouse has served as a navigational landmark for vessels near the river mouth.

Motorboat trips along the Preguiças River depart from Barreirinhas. The route gives visitors a chance to see the riverbanks, vegetation and daily life in the riverside settlements.

Excursions include Vassouras and fishing villages. The river journey complements a visit to the sand dunes of Lençóis Maranhenses.
